tone_statements.citation: Maddieson, Ian. 2013. Tone (chapter 13A), datapoint Yeyi. In Matthew S. Dryer & Martin Haspelmath (eds.), The World Atlas of Language Structures Online. Leipzig: MPI-EVA.
tone_statements.quote: Datapoint Yeyi / Tone. Language: Yeyi. Feature: Tone by Ian Maddieson. Value: Simple tone system. References: Gowlett 1997. [Chapter 13, sect. 2, defining the value:] The languages with tones are divided into those with a simple tone system — essentially those with only a two-way basic contrast, usually between high and low levels — and those with a more complex set of contrasts.

tone_statements.summary: WALS codes Yeyi (WALS code yey, ISO yey, Ngamiland) as having a simple tone system, i.e. a basic two-way (High vs Low) lexical tone contrast, coded second-hand from Gowlett 1997 'Aspects of Yeyi diachronic phonology'.

tone_statements.citation: Lusekelo, Amani. 2009. Review of Frank Seidel 2008, A Grammar of Yeyi. Afrikanistik online 2009: 1-5. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2009_3531
tone_statements.quote: The prosodology section of this chapter is quite detailed and mainly concentrates on an acoustically based analysis of Yeyi prosody. Shortly, the author demonstrates that Yeyi is characterized with High Tone (termed as Prosodeme II), Low Tone (Prosodeme I) which are semantically distinct (p. 57) and have grammatical functions (p. 61) as well as Prosodeme iii. I am aware that the issue of Bantu tone needs much attention which the author succeedes to manage. Furthermore, intonation is given in demarcative and expressive grounds.
tone_statements.locator: para. <4>, p. 2 (reviewing Seidel 2008 ch. 2 'prosodology', pp. 54-99, tone contrast p. 57, grammatical tone p. 61)

tone.says: Two tones, High and Low, lexically and grammatically contrastive (per a review of Seidel's 2008 grammar, whose analysis is acoustic); a third 'Prosodeme III' is named but not described.
